intro: Senegal, on Africa's westernmost tip, is known for its stable democracy, its music and its long history of trade.

chapters.title: Empires and kingdoms
text: Parts of Senegal belonged to the empires of Ghana, Mali and the Jolof (Wolof) Empire. The Senegambian stone circles, over 1,000 standing stones, are more than a thousand years old.
Islam spread through traders and later through Sufi brotherhoods that remain powerful today.

chapters.title: Gorée and French rule
text: Gorée Island off Dakar became a symbol of the Atlantic slave trade. France expanded from Saint-Louis in the 1800s, and Dakar became the capital of French West Africa.
Senegalese soldiers, the tirailleurs, fought for France in both world wars.

chapters.title: Independence and democracy
text: Senegal became independent in 1960 under the poet-president Léopold Sédar Senghor. It has never had a military coup. In 2024 Bassirou Diomaye Faye became Africa's youngest elected president at 44 after a tense election.

highlight.title: No coups
highlight.text: Senegal is one of the few West African countries never to have had a military coup.

keyTerms.meaning: A religious order, such as the Mourides.
